caveat: Thresholds are the Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) EDL engineering constraints from the JPL MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide (Feb/Apr 2006, 'working assumptions subject to future review'). They are a published NASA reference point, NOT the final Mars 2020 requirements: the Mars 2020 elevation and latitude limits could not be verified from a NASA page that was fetched and read, so they are omitted. Perseverance used Range Trigger and Terrain-Relative Navigation, which allow terrain that these constraints would reject.

guide.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide to Engineering Constraints (JPL, Apr 2006)

ellipse.azimuthNote: ASSUMPTION: the cited NASA pages give the ellipse size (7.7 km by 6.6 km, i.e. full axes) but not its orientation; 0 deg (major axis north-south) is an arbitrary default and can be overridden.

source.title: NASA Science: Perseverance Rover Landing Ellipse in Jezero Crater (4.8 by 4.1 miles, 7.7 by 6.6 km)

ellipse.quote: The landing ellipse, measuring 4.8 miles by 4.1 miles (7.7 kilometers by 6.6 kilometers)

verdictRule: meets-all = every criterion with required=true is evaluated and passes; fails-some = any evaluated criterion fails; otherwise insufficient-data. Criteria with required=false need rover-scale data the global dataset does not have and are listed with no verdict.

source.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide, section 1.2 Latitude
source.quote: MSL EDL is designed to land at any latitude between 60N and 60S.

criteria.label: Landing-site elevation (MOLA areoid)
criteria.limitText: elevation <= +2000 m above the MOLA areoid

source.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide, section 1.3 Altitude
source.quote: allowing the landing site altitude to be as high as +2 km with respect to the MOLA-defined areoid.

criteria.label: Regional slope (2-5 km length scale)
criteria.limitText: slope <= 3 deg over a 2-5 km length scale

source.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide, section 1.5 Slopes
source.quote: three degrees or less over a 2 to 5 km length scale to avoid altimetry errors in the start of powered descent

criteria.label: Thermal inertia (not dust-dominated)
criteria.limitText: thermal inertia > 100 J m-2 s-0.5 K-1

source.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide, section 3.3 Table 2 (Load bearing surface)
source.quote: Load bearing surface | Not dominated by dust | Thermal inertia >100 J m-2 s-0.5 K-1 and albedo <0.25

criteria.label: Slope at 200-500 m length scale
criteria.limitText: slope <= 5 deg over a 200-500 m length scale
criteria.unassessableReason: needs sub-kilometre topography (stereo or photoclinometry); the global DEM cannot resolve it

source.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide, section 1.5 Slopes
source.quote: five degrees or less over a 200 to 500 m length scale to avoid altimetry errors in preparation for the sky-crane landing maneuver

criteria.label: Slope at 20-40 m length scale
criteria.limitText: slope <= 15 deg over a 20-40 m length scale
criteria.unassessableReason: needs metre-scale topography; only available inside Jezero (20 m CTX DEM)

source.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide, section 1.5 Slopes
source.quote: fifteen degrees or less over a 20 to 40 m length scale to avoid altimetry errors in preparation for rover release

criteria.label: Slope at 5 m length scale
criteria.limitText: slope <= 15 deg over a 5 m length scale

source.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide, section 1.5 Slopes
source.quote: fifteen degrees or less over a 5 m length scale to ensure landing stability and trafficability of the rover

criteria.label: Rock abundance (damaging rocks under the rover)
criteria.limitText: rock abundance of around 10% or less (less than 0.25% chance of a rock taller than 0.6 m in a 4 m2 area)
criteria.unassessableReason: needs a rock-abundance map (thermal differencing or high-resolution imagery), which is not in the global dataset

source.title: MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide, section 1.6 Rocks
source.quote: this translates to a rock abundance (cumulative area covered by rocks) of around 10%.
